issue.title: [FEATURE] Enable/disable an automation or script without ha_call_service
issue.body:
### What would you like to see?

`ha_config_set_automation` and `ha_config_set_script` should accept an `enabled: bool | None` parameter that enables or disables the automation/script, routed internally to the appropriate service call rather than written into the stored config.

Right now there is no way to enable or disable an automation or a script through the automation/script tool surface. Every route is closed except `ha_call_service`:

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| `ha_config_set_automation` / `ha_config_set_script` | No `enabled` parameter. Passing `enabled: false` inside `config` is invalid — HA rejects unknown top-level keys at schema validation and the automation loads as `unavailable`. |
| `ha_set_entity(enabled=False)` | Refused by design: *"NOT allowed for automation or script entities — use `automation.turn_off` / `script.turn_off` via `ha_call_service()` instead."* |
| `ha_config_remove_automation` / `ha_config_remove_script` | Deletes it. Not a disable. |
| `ha_call_service("automation", "turn_off")` | Works — the only route. |

### Why do you need this?

Disabling an automation is routine, low-risk and fully reversible, but it is reachable only through the one tool most likely to be gated — `ha_call_service` is the universal actuator tool covering locks, covers, alarm panels and everything else. On an install that gates `ha_call_service` through Tool Security Policies, disabling an automation becomes impossible, while creating, rewriting and **deleting** that same automation stay available through `ha_config_set_automation` / `ha_config_remove_automation`.

That is inverted: the destructive operations are ungated, the reversible one is not.

It also costs an agent two wrong turns. The natural first guess is `ha_config_set_automation`; the second is `ha_set_entity(enabled=False)`; only the third works. `ha_set_entity`'s docstring does point at the right answer, but only once its schema is already loaded.

### Additional context

Suggested shape — one optional parameter on the existing tools rather than a new tool, per `.gemini/styleguide.md` § *Tool Consolidation and Module Size*:

```python
enabled: bool | None = None
# None (default) -> no change
# True           -> turn on
# False          -> turn off
```

- Must **not** write `enabled:` into the stored config. The bundled best-practices skill (`references/automation-patterns.md` § *Disabling Automations*) documents that `enabled:` is not a valid top-level key. (`enabled:` on an individual trigger/condition/action is valid and unrelated.)
- Should work standalone — `identifier` + `enabled`, with no `config` or `python_transform` — so "just disable this" is one call.
- **Open design question for scripts:** `automation.turn_off` disables an automation's triggers, which is what the Automations-page toggle does. `script.turn_off` is not the same operation — it stops a running script rather than disabling it, so the script equivalent of an automation disable may only exist at registry level. Worth deciding whether `enabled` on `ha_config_set_script` means "stop the running script", "registry-disable", or whether the parameter should land on `ha_config_set_automation` only. Note that `ha_set_entity`'s refusal message currently points scripts at `script.turn_off` as though it were equivalent.
- Registry-level disable (`config/entity_registry/update` with `disabled_by: user`) has different persistence semantics — the entity leaves the state machine entirely — and is a separate decision from the state-machine toggle.
- Adding a parameter is not breaking per the styleguide's *Breaking Changes* section.

---

### Addendum

This report was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Opus), which has been unreliable lately. Treat every claim, table entry and suggestion above as unverified — confirm the tool behaviour, the schema constraints and the proposed design against current source before acting on any of it.

comments.body:
I traced the open script question against current Home Assistant Core (`f8e8e03f`). The two domains do not have equivalent service semantics:

- [`automation.async_turn_on` / `async_turn_off`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8e8e03f430bfcb4a16e21a2640049ac505754ad/homeassistant/components/automation/__init__.py#L661-L674) toggle the automation's `_is_enabled` state and attach/detach triggers, so `enabled` maps cleanly to `automation.turn_on` / `automation.turn_off`.
- [`script.turn_on`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8e8e03f430bfcb4a16e21a2640049ac505754ad/homeassistant/components/script/__init__.py#L236-L243) starts a run, while [`script.turn_off`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8e8e03f430bfcb4a16e21a2640049ac505754ad/homeassistant/components/script/__init__.py#L245-L260) only cancels active runs. Calling either from `ha_config_set_script(enabled=...)` would execute/stop a script, not enable/disable it.
- Registry disable is a separate admin-only operation: `config/entity_registry/update` accepts only `disabled_by: user|None`, and re-enabling may require a config-entry reload or restart ([Core source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8e8e03f430bfcb4a16e21a2640049ac505754ad/homeassistant/components/config/entity_registry.py#L175-L182), [reload behavior](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8e8e03f430bfcb4a16e21a2640049ac505754ad/homeassistant/components/config/entity_registry.py#L291-L300)). That is materially different from an automation state toggle.

My recommendation is the narrow contract first: add `enabled: bool | None` to `ha_config_set_automation` only, support standalone `identifier + enabled`, never write it into config, and apply the service call after an optional config/transform write has registered the entity. The existing `wait` flag can cover verification of the final `on`/`off` state. Leave `ha_config_set_script` unchanged and correct `ha_set_entity`'s script guidance, since its current `script.turn_off` suggestion conflates stopping with disabling.

If registry-level script disabling is desired, I think it needs an explicit contract (admin requirement, entity disappearance, reload/restart result) rather than sharing this boolean. I can implement the automation-only scope once that boundary is confirmed.

@Elioooon I agree with your recommendation, if you want to make the PR feel free. Since it's such a small change you can do both the addition to set automation and the change to set entity script guidance in one PR, no need to implement registry level script disabling.
